text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: network: detected elevated packet loss and route churn to upstream ASN 64555 affecting eu-west egress (multiple AZs). Paging SRE rotation now.

alex: getting alerts — BGP monitor shows rapid withdraw/announce from 203.0.113.1 (peer AS64555). Loss spiking to 30% for next-hop paths.

jin: joining. which services impacted?

support-eng: we have multiple customer reports for embeddings and streaming gen in eu-west-1 — elevated latencies and intermittent 502/504s since ~10:05 UTC.

maya: seeing similar in telemetry — p95 token latency up 3x for eu-west routes routed via provider-64555. Other providers look normal.

ops-lead: quick checklist: 1) confirm scope (regions/AZ), 2) triage pub routes, 3) call provider NOC, 4) temporary traffic steering. who's oncall?

sre-rotation: that's me. I'm taking lead. starting traceroutes and BGP dumps.

alex: pasting diagnostics:
```
# traceroute to 13.59.12.7 (eu-west svc node)
1 10.0.0.1 0.5 ms
2 198.51.100.1 5.2 ms
3 203.0.113.1 120 ms (30% loss)
4 * * *
```

alex: bgp neighbor summary to AS64555: neighbor 203.0.113.1 -> state established, but prefixes flapping, withdraws frequent.

jin: running BGP table diff now. If provider is oscillating, we should prefer backup provider via local-pref flip for eu-west to pull traffic off the flaky path.

ops-lead: execute traffic steering plan, but coordinate with peering-noc before making big changes. Also inform support to message impacted customers.

peering-noc: I'm on the provider side channel now. Provider sees a hardware interface on their PE flapping, causing route withdraws; they're replacing the interface. They request we avoid prefix churn by not re-announcing specifics until they stabilize.

jin: ok — plan A: raise local-preference for backup-provider neighbor to 200 for eu-west only; Plan B if churn continues: temporarily blackhole specific high-volume prefixes to avoid backend overload (last resort).

maya: creating a quick route-map:
```
route-map PREFER-BACKUP permit 10
 match ip address prefix-list EUWEST
 set local-preference 200
```
apply to neighbor 198.51.100.2 (backup provider). Deploying in 2 mins.

sre-rotation: applying now to edge routers in eu-west. rolling across AZs: az1 -> az2 -> az3, 30s pauses.

alex: applied in az1, traffic shifted ~40% away from AS64555, packet loss on egress decreased to 6% on az1.

peering-noc: provider reported they have a replacement scheduled and should see stable adj in ~15-20 minutes. they're continuing diagnostics on their transport.

support-eng: posting customer-facing update: "We are investigating increased latency and errors in eu-west. Traffic is being rerouted to maintain service — may see reduced capacity for a short period."

pm-ricardo: queueing a post-incident note for affected customers and flagging enterprise seats that have strict SLAs.

ops-lead: creating INCIDENT-7891 in tracker, severity = SEV-2 while provider fixes. Assigning to jin and peering-noc.

jin: continuing to monitor BGP RIB, also verifying KV/connection cache behavior after path changes to make sure model inferences aren't timing out.

alex: metric update: overall request error-rate for embeddings-api in eu-west peaked at 4.8% and is down to 0.9% after reroute. latency p95 back to ~1.2x baseline.

peering-noc: provider reports replacement complete; adj stable for ~8 minutes, no more withdraw storms from their side.

sre-rotation: rolling back local-pref to normal over next 5 mins and observing.

maya: rollback complete in az1, az2; traffic naturally moved back, packet loss remains low (<1%).

support-eng: customers reporting improvements, a few say full recovery. leaving support page open for follow-ups.

ops-lead: good. reduce severity to SEV-3. Jin, please run a follow-up with provider to get RCA and ensure we have a permanent peering mitigation (e.g., BFD timers, dampening).

jin: will open RFC with network team and schedule peering runbook updates. also will capture BGP logs and export to incident binder.

peering-noc: provider committed to upgrade QA on that POP. they'll send RCA within 48 hours.

ops-lead: summary for the record: root cause = flapping HW interface in upstream provider AS64555 causing repeated BGP withdraws; mitigation = temporary local-pref shift to backup provider, monitored rollback after stabilization; impact = increased latency and client errors for eu-west gen/embeddings for ~25 minutes, partially mitigated by reroute; customers mostly recovered.

pm-ricardo: scheduling postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:00 UTC with peering/contact owners and product.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident INC-7891 status changed: mitigated -> monitoring.

sre-rotation: handing pager to next rotation in 20m, leaving runbook notes in the incident.

support-eng: will send final customer follow-up once RCA received.

pm-ricardo: thanks team — good coordination.
